##: This is the source copy. The bucket Scoop actually reads from is
mumudevx/scoop-dpb (`scoop bucket add dpb https://github.com/mumudevx/scoop-dpb`,
then `scoop install dpb`); this file is checked in here so the manifest is
version-controlled with the code that produces the archives it points at,
the same reasoning Formula/dpb.rb gives for keeping a copy in-repo.
URLs use the GitHub REPOSITORY slug, dpi-bypass-mac, not the Go module path
github.com/mumudevx/dpb -- the module was never renamed to match the repo.
Confirmed against .goreleaser.yaml's release.github block (owner: mumudevx,
name: dpi-bypass-mac). Getting this wrong is not hypothetical: it already
produced one real `brew install` 404 in this project.
version/url below match the v0.1.0 tag; the two `hash` values are 64-zero
placeholders, not real checksums -- no windows_amd64.zip / windows_arm64.zip
has actually been published under that tag yet. Before this manifest is
pushed to mumudevx/scoop-dpb for a real cut: bump `version`, drop the
-SNAPSHOT-<commit> suffix goreleaser adds outside of a real tag build, and
replace both `hash` values with the sha256 lines from that release's
checksums.txt (`https://github.com/mumudevx/dpi-bypass-mac/releases/download/v<version>/checksums.txt`) --
same source Formula/dpb.rb's header points at for the macOS side.
dpb.exe is unsigned. Scoop does not suppress SmartScreen for an unsigned
binary any more than a direct download does; see README.md's Windows
section for what the warning looks like and how to proceed.
description: DPI bypass for Windows and macOS: connects plain first, desyncs only on evidence
notes: dpb.exe is not code-signed. Windows SmartScreen will still warn on first run -- verify the SHA256 against that release's checksums.txt before running it, the same check README.md asks for on a direct download.
